title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, 2nd draft, June 1986). Grothendieck is axiomatising a category 𝓕 of 'figures', meaning tame or polyhedral-type spaces given with a cell or stratification structure. Each figure F has an associated ordered set F̃ of elementary pieces. On the next page these are called 'multitubulaires'; they behave like closed cells. Subfigures of F correspond to certain subsets of F̃. A refinement (subdivision) F' ≪ F comes with a canonical order map φ: F̃' → F̃. By Corollary 2 on p.66, pulling back subfigures along φ (G ↦ F'.G = φ^{-1}(G)) commutes with Sup and Inf.

This page finishes Corollary 3. Take F' ≪ F and a covering family of subfigures F = Sup F_i (notation ∨F_i), with F_ij = F_i ∧ F_j. Let F'_i, F'_ij be the induced subfigures of F'. Then:
(i) each F'_i is a refinement of F_i;
(ii) the refinement that F'_i induces on F_ij is F'_ij, and this equals the one induced by F'_j;
(iii) F' = Sup F'_i, and F' is a refinement of F.

The margin NB says the following. If one is only given F'_i ≪ F_i with F'_i|F_ij = F'_j|F_ij, then (iii) says a refinement F' restricting to them is determined: F'|F_ij = F'_ij.

This yields a 'principe de recollement'. Refinements of F are determined by a compatible family of refinements of the pieces F_i. In modern terms, U ↦ {refinements of U} is a separated presheaf on the lattice of subfigures. The open question is existence: can an arbitrary compatible family be glued?

That is imposed as an axiom, AR (Axiome de recollement des raffinements). Let F ∈ 𝓕. For each X ∈ F̃ choose a refinement F'_X ≪ X, such that F'_Y = F'_X|Y whenever Y ≤ X. Then there exists F' ≪ F with F'|X = F'_X for all X ∈ F̃. Uniqueness follows from Corollary 3 and is stated on p.68.

In modern language this is the sheaf (gluing) condition for subdivisions over the face poset with its Alexandrov topology. It is the familiar PL / cell-complex fact that compatible subdivisions of the closed cells of a complex assemble into a subdivision of the whole. The next page notes the real difficulty: comparing F'_X and F'_Y when X and Y are incomparable. It then proposes a slightly weaker variant axiom.
errors: The axiom asks for compatibility only along comparable pairs Y ≤ X. For incomparable cells, compatibility on X∩Y follows only if X∩Y is a union (Sup) of cells below both and restrictions behave well. Grothendieck flags exactly this gap on p.68, so it is acknowledged rather than an error.
For infinite F̃, forming Sup F'_X is not automatic; p.68 notes this too. The axiom deliberately absorbs the existence problem.

ideas.what: Restricting a refinement to a covering family of subfigures yields compatible refinements of the pieces, and the refinement is the Sup of its restrictions
ideas.modern_name: separated presheaf (locality) property of subdivisions over a cover by subcomplexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in PL topology (cf. Rourke–Sanderson, Zeeman)

ideas.what: Axiom AR: compatible refinements of each elementary cell X ∈ F̃ glue to a refinement of F
ideas.modern_name: gluing/sheaf condition for subdivisions on the face poset (Alexandrov topology); extension of subdivisions cell by cell
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in PL / polyhedral complexes theory; axiomatic tame-topology framework only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5
ideas.where_published: Tame topology program announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this axiomatics is unpublished

missed.claim: Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic 'figures' framework for tame topology treats refinements as a sheaf over the poset F̃ of elementary cells, with gluing taken as an axiom. This is a small, concrete piece of the never-published tame-topology foundations, but the mathematics itself is standard PL folklore.
missed.quote: AR (Axiome de recollement des raffinements) Soit F ∈ 𝓕, et pour tout raffinement X ∈ F̃, soit F'_X ≪ X un raffinement de X.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents how Grothendieck intended to build tame topology axiomatically, in parallel with o-minimality and stratified spaces. This is of historical interest, not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine gluing / sheaf property of subdivisions inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. It has historical interest for the tame-topology program, but no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The conclusion of the axiom should read 'Alors ∃ F' ≪ F' (the superscript X near the tilde is a stray mark or correction), i.e. ∃ F' ≪ F such that F'_X = F'|X for all X ∈ F̃.
In the axiom statement, 'pour tout raffinement X ∈ F̃' is likely 'pour tout X ∈ F̃' (X ranges over elementary pieces, not refinements); the word 'raffinement' attaches to F'_X.
The axiom label is hard to read ('A I M' / 'At W' in the image). The parenthetical clearly says 'Axiome de recollement des raffinements'.
The margin note reads roughly: 'NB Si l'on se donne des F'_i tels que F'_i|F_ij = F'_j|F_ij, alors (iii) signifie que F'|F_ij = F'_ij'.
Line 3 is struck through: 'F' = Sup F'_i, F'_i ∩ F'_j = F'_ij'.
